page.layout: One printed page: running head and page number at the top; two portrait medallions (woodcuts) in the upper part; one column of running text below them; signature at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: CHRISTIERNVS Ioannis Daniæ Regis filius, post patris obitum Danorum Rex, nullum non lapidem mouit quo regnum Suecię suo regno adiiceret: quod & tandem partim vi armorum, partim dolo assecutus est: sed tamē non diu administrauit: quinimo tantum abest vt retinere potuerit, vt etiam patrio ac peculiari suo regno Daniæ ob tyrānidem deturbaretur, atque exul in Angliam vnà cū vxore profugeret, anno à mundo condito 5484. à Christo nato 1522. Cæterum cùm Daniam recuperare tentaret, à Christiano, patruo suo, captus est, atque in carcerem cõiectus, vbi diem clausit extremum. Vide Cosmog. Mun. li.4. de regnis Septentrionalibus: item nouam temporum continuationem Germani cuiusdam, ad Euse.Chro. adiectam: præterea Carionis Chro. li.3. qui loco Daniæ scribit Regē Christiernum Daciæ: vnde colligendum Daniam, & Daciam, interim confundi, nam & Volater. li. 7. sic inquit: Nunc sanè Cimbricam Chersonesum Daciam vocant, cui Rex præest qui Suetiam & Noruegiam, peninsulas, in eodem mari obtinet, Ptolemæo & antiquis minimè positas, quòd ignotæ atque incompertæ tunc essent.

ISABELLA Caroli Imperatoris huius nominis quinti soror, nupsit Christierno Danię Regi supradicto, qui ex ea liberos sustulit, Dorotheam Friderici Palatini vxorem, & Christianam, Lotharingiæ Ducissam. Vide vt suprà.

page.notes: The two medallions at the top are woodcut portraits with legends printed in them: left "CHRIS III REX DA." (Christiernus III, King of Denmark) and right "ELIZABET R. DA." (Elizabeth, Queen of Denmark). Not transcribed as running text; they are illustrations. The page number "233" is printed at the top right, set in an old-style figure. In the signature the final figure is printed in an unusual form, read here as 5.
